_**Law of the Plainsman**_ is a Western television series starring Michael Ansara that aired on NBC from October 1, 1959, until September 22, 1960.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-slts-1)
The character of Native American Deputy U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart was introduced in two episodes ("The Indian" and "The Raid") of the popular ABC Western television series _The Rifleman_ starring Chuck Connors. As with _The Rifleman_, this series was produced by Four Star Productions in association with Levy-Gardner-Laven Productions.
_Law of the Plainsman_ is distinctive in that it was one of the few television programs that featured a Native American as the lead character, a bold move for American network television at that time. Ansara had earlier appeared in the series _Broken Arrow_, having portrayed the Apache chief, Cochise. Ansara played Sam Buckhart, an Apache Indian who saved the life of a U.S. Cavalry officer after an Indian ambush. When the officer later died, he left Sam money that was used for an education at private schools and Harvard University. ## Law of the Plainsman(1959)
### Overview
Law of the Plainsman is a Western television series starring Michael Ansara that aired on the NBC television network from October 1, 1959, until May 5, 1960. The character of Native American U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart was introduced in two episodes of the popular ABC Western television series The Rifleman starring Chuck Connors as Lucas McCain.
Law of the Plainsman is distinctive and unique in that it was one of the few television programs that featured a Native American as the lead character, a bold move for U.S.network television at that time. Ansara had earlier appeared in the series Broken Arrow, having portrayed the Apache chief, Cochise. Ansara, however, was not Native American but of Syrian descent.
Ansara played Sam Buckhart, an Apache Indian who saved the life of a U.S. Cavalry officer after an Indian ambush. When the officer died, he left Sam money that was used for an education at private schools and Harvard University. After school, he returned to New Mexico where he became a Deputy Marshal working for Marshal Andy Morrison. He lived in a boarding house run by Martha Commager. The only other continuing character was 8-year old Tess Logan, an orphan who had been rescued by Buckhart. Robert Harland, later of Target: The Corruptors! starred in seven episodes as Deputy Billy Lordan. Wayne Rogers, who went on to star in another Four Star western, Stagecoach West, and later, MAS*H, also played deputy Lordan in several episodes.

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_, is a reality televisionspin-off series of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_ created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") The series began on February 7, 2018, on CBS in the United States and is simulcast in Canada on Global. The series is filmed at CBS Studio Center in sound stage eighteen located in Studio City, Los Angeles. Julie Chen Moonves reprises her role as host from _Big Brother_ with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan also returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.
The premise of the series remained largely unchanged from the main edition of _Big Brother_, in which a group of contestants, known as "HouseGuests," who live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother House, with no contact from the outside world. The contestants compete in competitions for safety and for power over the household before voting each other out in an attempt to be the last HouseGuest remaining and win a grand prize. The difference from the parent series is the inclusion of "Celebrity" HouseGuests (those with notoriety prior to participating in the series), the time frame (a month as opposed to 3 months) and a smaller grand prize ($250,000 as opposed to $750,000)
Each season is also transmitted in real-time which allows for greater viewer participation in the form of _America's Vote_ where the public can give their favorite HouseGuest various prizes ranging from luxury items to advantage to help them survive inside the House. Prior to the live season finale, the viewers are able to vote for their _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with the winner getting an auxiliary prize of $25,000.

The first overall season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ worldwide premiered in the United Kingdom in 2001 while an American version of the format has been speculated since 2002. The first season of the American adaptation was announced during a live double eviction episode of the nineteenth regular season on September 7, 2017, by Julie Chen Moonves. The first season was scheduled during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The series premiere was the number one program for CBS attracting 7.27 million viewers and the highest-rated season premiere since _Big Brother 13_. The program was often covered in the media due to the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her political revelations in the first season.
In September 2021, CBS renewed _Celebrity Big Brother_ for a third season, which premiered on February 2, 2022.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Air_date-1)
In October 2025, CBS cancelled _Celebrity Big Brother_ after three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)

The series is a game show in which a group of celebrity contestants, referred to as HouseGuests, live in a custom-built set, known as the Big Brother House, constantly under video surveillance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3) While in the House, the HouseGuests are completely isolated from the outside world, meaning no phone, television, Internet, magazines, newspaper, or contact with those not in the House.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) This rule could be broken, however, in the event of a medical injury, a family emergency, or death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) The format of the series is mainly seen as a social experiment, and requires HouseGuests to interact with others who may have differing ideals, beliefs, and prejudices.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3.2-6) Though locked in the House, the HouseGuests are free to quit the game, though will not be allowed entry back into the game.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-4-7) Should a HouseGuest break the rules of the game, they could be expelled from the House,

and unable to return.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-5-8) The HouseGuests compete for a grand prize of $250,000 and the runner-up is awarded $50,000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9) Prior to the live finale the viewers are able to award their favorite HouseGuest of the season the title _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with a cash prize of $25,000.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9)

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-1) is a spin-off series of the American version of the Dutch reality television franchise _Big Brother_. This season aired during the winter of the 2017–18 network television season on CBS and was the second American _Big Brother_ season to air outside the usual summer television season, the first being _Big Brother 9_ in 2008. Julie Chen returned as host, with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America. The first season premiered on February 7, 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvline-2)

The promotional logo was released on December 20, 2017. The logo is similar to that used for _Big Brother 19_, with the word "celebrity" added.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-3) The first teaser was also released the same day.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-4) In January 2018 official photos of the house and backyard were released through a press release and an Instagram livestream with Julie Chen.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-6) On January 28, 2018, the official cast was announced during the 60th Annual Grammy Awards.
The first season officially concluded on February 25, 2018, when Marissa Jaret Winokur beat Ross Mathews by a final jury vote of 6 to 3. Ross was also later named _America's Favorite HouseGuest_.
On May 12, 2018, CBS renewed the spin-off for a second season.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-7)

After the first season of the British version of _Big Brother_ proved to be a success in the ratings for Channel 4, the network collaborated with the BBC for the first British season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ in aid of Comic Relief. The season ran for a condensed run of eight days and featured six British celebrities moving into the house used for the first British season.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-42) Due to the success of the first celebrity edition, a second season was ordered and shown exclusively on Channel 4 in November 2002. The celebrity version took a two-year break before returning for its third season in 2005, and became a regular staple alongside the regular British version. Starting with the third season, the show began to feature celebrities outside the United Kingdom alongside well known British celebrities. Many notable American celebrities have since taken part in the British version of _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-GlobalTV-43)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-AmericansInUKCBB-2-44) American actor Gary Busey took part in the fourteenth season in the summer of 2014 and became the first American celebrity to win _Celebrity Big Brother_ in the United Kingdom._[citation needed_]

An American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ has been speculated since 2002, along with a celebrity version of _Survivor._[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-CBB-2002-1-45) In an interview, Julie Chen and CBS CEO Leslie Moonves revealed talks of a celebrity edition of _Big Brother_ as far back as _Big Brother 2._[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-46) It was rumored that CBS was looking to air a celebrity edition in the fall after _Big Brother 3_ with radio personality Howard Stern speculated as a possible houseguest.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-CBB-2002-2-47) Chen revealed that Paris Hilton had agreed to do it and Roseanne Barr initially agreed to take part, but then backed out.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-46) Barr would later take part in another celebrity spin-off of _Big Brother_ called _Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack_ in the United Kingdom in 2008, where she watched over a group of non-celebrity housemates for a day, set tasks and talked to them in the Diary Room.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Roseanne-BBCH-48)

Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018. CBS later confirmed via a press release that Julie Chen would return to host the new season, and Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan will be executive producers. The season will be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)
On September 13, 2017, it was revealed by Chen that her husband, CBS chief executive Leslie Moonves, forced her to take a pay cut for the celebrity edition to happen. Moonves stated, "You shouldn't be expected to be paid as if it's a full series. It's a condensed version."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)
The format of the show remained similar to the American version of _Big Brother_. Competitions for Head of Household and Power of Veto had been confirmed to returned for this edition along with live evictions.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvline-2) On December 1, 2017, CBS revealed that the series would premiere on February 7, 2018, and wrap on February 25, 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-51)

_Celebrity Big Brother_ was a condensed version of the game and would not last as long as a regular season of _Big Brother_, with episodes only shown over two weeks instead of three months.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-tvguide-50)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-52) Unlike the parent series Jury members were not sequestered separately and were allowed to return to the outside world as well as watch the show.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-53)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-54) Beginning with an incident that led to a lawsuit in _Big Brother 2_ when HouseGuest Justin Sebik got drunk and threatened fellow HouseGuest Krista Stegall by holding a knife to her throat, there has been an alcohol restriction in the house.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-56) The alcohol restriction was lifted for the Celebrity HouseGuests.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-57)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-58) The space in the backyard was reduced to allow production to constantly perform construction for competitions but still allow 24/7 access for the HouseGuests.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-59) For the celebrity version of America's Favorite HouseGuest,

the term Favorite Celebrity HouseGuest was also being used interchangeably.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-60)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-61) For the first time since the beginning of the American series, five players were featured in the season's finale night versus the usual three.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-62)

The main television coverage of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was screened on CBS during the winter of the 2017–18 network television season. CBS decided to schedule the spin-off during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49) Episodes aired on Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays with two special episodes on Thursday, February 8 and Saturday, February 24. Most episodes aired for one hour and aired from 8:00–9:00 p.m. EST; the Friday episodes and the season finale, however, ran for two hours each (from 8:00–10:00 p.m. EST).[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Air_dates-63) The live Internet feeds returned for the American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ as part of CBS All Access.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-46) Alongside the weekly shows on CBS, the companion series _Big Brother: After Dark_ returned on Pop under the title _Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_. The show provided live coverage nightly from inside the House.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Press1-49)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-64)

#### International broadcasts
[edit]
Promotional logo created for use in Australia that resembles the logo of Australian adaptation of _Big Brother_ from 2012 to 2014.
Global announced on December 20, 2017, that the broadcaster had acquired the rights to air _Celebrity Big Brother_ in Canada.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Broadcast-GlobalCAN-65) Global has broadcast the American version of _Big Brother_ since its launch in 2000.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-BBCPR-66)Nine Network confirmed they would air the season in Australia under the name _Celebrity Big Brother U.S._.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Australia-1-67) Nine created a special logo for the show resembling the eye logo of the ninth through eleventh seasons of Australian adaptation that previously aired on the network.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-68) Episodes were "fast-tracked" and available on their streaming service 9Now shortly after their American airing with televised broadcast on 9Go! starting February 11, 2018.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-Australia-1-67) Due to low ratings episodes were moved from the 9:30pm timeslot to 11:30pm effective February 14, 2018.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_1_(American_season)#cite_note-69)

Many notable American celebrities have since taken part in the British version of _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-GlobalTV-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-AmericansInUKCBB-2-26) American actor Gary Busey took part in the fourteenth season in the summer of 2014 and became the first American celebrity to win _Celebrity Big Brother_ in the United Kingdom.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-Gary_Wins-27)
Julie Chen Moonves has hosted the series since its premiere.

### Differences from _Big Brother_
An American version of _Celebrity Big Brother_ has been speculated since 2002, along with a celebrity version of _Survivor._[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-2002-1-28) In an interview, Julie Chen and then CEO of CBS Corporation Leslie Moonves revealed talks of a celebrity edition of _Big Brother_ as far back as _Big Brother 2._[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-29) It was rumored that CBS was looking to air a celebrity edition in the fall after _Big Brother 3_ with radio personality Howard Stern speculated as a possible Houseguest.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB-2002-2-30) Chen revealed that Paris Hilton had agreed to do it and Roseanne Barr initially agreed to take part, but then backed out.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-InterviewTHR-29) Barr would later take part in another celebrity spin-off of _Big Brother_ called _Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack_ in the United Kingdom in 2008, where she watched over a group of non-celebrity housemates for a day, set tasks and talked to them in the Diary Room.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Roseanne-BBCH-31) Julie Chen announced on September 7, 2017, during a live double eviction episode of _Big Brother 19_ that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would air sometime during the winter, before the twentieth season of _Big Brother_ in the summer of 2018.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-32)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
CBS confirmed that Chen would reprise her role as host for the celebrity edition with executive producers Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan returning. CBS also confirmed that the celebrity edition would be produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Press1-33) In an interview Chen revealed that her husband Les Moonves forced her to take a pay cut for _Celebrity Big Brother_ due to it being a condensed version.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-tvguide-34) Chen returned as the host for the second season now being credited as Julie Chen Moonves.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-JCReturn-35)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
Don Wollman and Clayton Halsey also reprises their roles as a co-executive producer and editor respectively.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits-36) Wollman also serves as the voice of Big Brother where he pre-records a series of statements that are played over the loud speakers inside the House. These range from asking HouseGuests to come to the Diary Room or reminding them they are not allowed to talk about production and their Diary Room sessions with other HouseGuests. Occasionally Wollman will make announcements to the HouseGuests that are not pre-recorded. Wollman's voice is primarily heard on the live Internet feeds while occasionally heard on the episodes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-41) Halsey also serves as the narrator for the opening and closings of the broadcast episodes. In this role he recaps recent events that were aired in previous episodes during the opening while explaining what events will take place in future episodes during the closing.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Voices-38)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits2-37)

### Differences from _Big Brother_

### Production design and music
_Celebrity Big Brother_ was not mentioned when CBS announced their plans for the 2019–20 television season on May 15, 2019.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-59)Kelly Kahl, president of entertainment at CBS, revealed on May 21, 2019 that a third season of the celebrity spin-off is still uncertain.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-60) On September 5, 2019 the parent series _Big Brother_ was renewed for a twenty-second season with Chen Moonves signing a new contract to return as host.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-61) However the new contract for Chen Moonves did not include a future season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ with CBS not announcing anything official regarding the series.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-62) On November 11, 2019, CBS announced their 2020 winter schedule, which did not include _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-63) On December 28, 2020, Chen Moonves revealed that shortly after the conclusion of the twenty-second season of the civilian version of _Big Brother_ that she and numerous producers pushed CBS to order a third season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ but that they declined to order one at the time leaving the option open to still order a third season at a later date.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-64)

A third season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ was officially announced on September 9, 2021, for Winter 2022 with Julie Chen Moonves returning as host.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-65)

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_, is a reality televisionspin-off series of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_ created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") The series began on February 7, 2018, on CBS in the United States and is simulcast in Canada on Global. The series is filmed at CBS Studio Center in sound stage eighteen located in Studio City, Los Angeles. Julie Chen Moonves reprises her role as host from _Big Brother_ with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan also returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.
The premise of the series remained largely unchanged from the main edition of _Big Brother_, in which a group of contestants, known as "HouseGuests," who live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother House, with no contact from the outside world. The contestants compete in competitions for safety and for power over the household before voting each other out in an attempt to be the last HouseGuest remaining and win a grand prize. The difference from the parent series is the inclusion of "Celebrity" HouseGuests (those with notoriety prior to participating in the series), the time frame (a month as opposed to 3 months) and a smaller grand prize ($250,000 as opposed to $750,000)
Each season is also transmitted in real-time which allows for greater viewer participation in the form of _America's Vote_ where the public can give their favorite HouseGuest various prizes ranging from luxury items to advantage to help them survive inside the House. Prior to the live season finale, the viewers are able to vote for their _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with the winner getting an auxiliary prize of $25,000.

The first overall season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ worldwide premiered in the United Kingdom in 2001 while an American version of the format has been speculated since 2002. The first season of the American adaptation was announced during a live double eviction episode of the nineteenth regular season on September 7, 2017, by Julie Chen Moonves. The first season was scheduled during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The series premiere was the number one program for CBS attracting 7.27 million viewers and the highest-rated season premiere since _Big Brother 13_. The program was often covered in the media due to the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her political revelations in the first season.
In September 2021, CBS renewed _Celebrity Big Brother_ for a third season, which premiered on February 2, 2022.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Air_date-1)
In October 2025, CBS cancelled _Celebrity Big Brother_ after three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)
texts.3: The series is a game show in which a group of celebrity contestants, referred to as HouseGuests, live in a custom-built set, known as the Big Brother House, constantly under video surveillance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3) While in the House, the HouseGuests are completely isolated from the outside world, meaning no phone, television, Internet, magazines, newspaper, or contact with those not in the House.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) This rule could be broken, however, in the event of a medical injury, a family emergency, or death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) The format of the series is mainly seen as a social experiment, and requires HouseGuests to interact with others who may have differing ideals, beliefs, and prejudices.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3.2-6) Though locked in the House, the HouseGuests are free to quit the game, though will not be allowed entry back into the game.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-4-7) Should a HouseGuest break the rules of the game, they could be expelled from the House,
